newsitem.title: UK: Britain's Labour says no going back on union reforms.
newsitem.headline: Britain's Labour says no going back on union reforms.

text.p: Gordon Brown, finance spokesman for Britain's opposition Labour Party, said on Tuesday there would be no reversal of trade union reforms introduced by the Conservative government in the 1980s.
"There is no turning back to the union legislation of the 1970s. There is no proposal to do so and we will be quite explicit in our manifesto," he told reporters.
Brown said strike ballots would be retained along with legislation protecting the right to be, or not to be, a union member.
"That is part of our proposal. There is no return to the old ways."

Brown was responding to comments made earlier by deputy prime minister Michael Heseltine who attacked the Labour Party's relationship with trade unions and said it had become a central issue in the May 1 election campaign.
"Companies will become battle grounds in which different unions with separate agendas fight out historic rivalries and enmities, each seeking their own toehold on power," Heseltine said.
